artist_scope: full contract (Tier 2, the simple-cyclic class: geckolib_migration_design.md section 5)
character_sheet: A small passive parrot in one of six plumages: a boxy body and head with a beak, a three-feather crest, three tail feathers, two jointed wings and two legs. It flies up when disturbed, breeds, and can be tamed and carried. Read it as a bright, restless little bird: wings beating, crest and tail never quite still.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.75 of the rig on a 64x32 sheet; six textures (bird1..bird6) by bird type.

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: roots: -/+1.5 rad offset, then pi x 0.35 = 1.100 rad (63 deg); tips: pi x 0.35
groups.plain: the wing roots beat about the body's long axis around a raised rest, the wing tips follow with the same shape and no offset; left and right mirrored
groups.math: lwing1.zRot = -1.5 + c; lwing2.zRot = c; rwing1.zRot = 1.5 - c; rwing2.zRot = -c, with c = cos(ageInTicks * 1.5 * 1.0) * pi * 0.35
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.5 x 1 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.5

groups.name: tail
groups.plain: the three tail feathers rock slowly up and down together
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.3 x 1 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.3

groups.name: feather1
groups.plain: the front crest feather sways side to side
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.1 x 1 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.1

groups.name: feather2
groups.plain: the middle crest feather sways a little faster
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.2 x 1 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.2

groups.name: feather3
groups.plain: the back crest feather sways faster still
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x 1 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.3

behaviour: Several independent rhythms run at all times, none scaled by walking speed; the classic code has no rest pose. The transcription ships idle (no bone) plus one clip per rhythm: the primary group (`primary_group`; the first group when the seed names none) carries the bare `walk` - a label, not a semantic: the contract's fly -> walk fallback is what plays a flyer's walk in flight (owner 2026-09-13, addendum item 26 (2)) - and every other rhythm is `walk_<group>`, so the GeckoLib candidate plays the transcription behind the switch.

Five rhythms: the wing beat (the primary group: its clip is the bare walk), the slow tail rock and three crest feathers each at its own sway; body, head, beak and legs are static. The wing roots bind at -1.561 / 1.595 rad and the formula re-centres them at -/+1.5, so the transcription's keys carry that offset (base minus bind).

The default renderer poses it from the classic code; the GeckoLib candidate sits behind the dev switch (-Dorespawn.dev.geckolibRenderers) and your clips replace the shipped transcription file for file.

clips.name: idle
clips.note: required with walk (today the transcription's idle keys no bone); a real perch: wings folded, crest and tail alive

clips.name: walk
clips.note: the wing beat (the primary group's transcription; a label, not a semantic)

clips.note: ruled 2026-09-06, Q3 (a): the vanilla death flip stays; a creature whose JSON ships a `death` clip gets the clip-replaces-flip mode, designed when the first such clip arrives (the Queen's own death clip the precedent) — a `death` delivered here plays under the flip until then
